Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to travel out to Stockholm University to Studenthuset to get my student log-in and register at home afterwards.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A student working at the desk. He was very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on fika's in the inner city near Östermalm, visit Kungsholmen for long walks along the mälar (water), go to Fotografiska or the National Museum.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, since I'm Danish and our culture and language are very close to the Swedish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Systembolaget, because I'm Danish (I guess), also, the clubs closes early, more governmental control in the streets, subways and such.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Fika, AW, mys, bullar, the people, the beautiful city, the architecture, the language. Everything.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Be prepared to seek social activities yourself. Stockholm University is very big and it feels pretty anonymous to be a student there, like it can on University of Copenhagen. 2) Prepare yourself mentally for a lot of planning and coordination yourself. I was unpleasantly surprised when I found out how much work it is to go abroad. There is a million deadlines you have to be aware of, you have to plan everything yourself (e.g. housing, courses). 3) Apply for as many scholarships as possible. It is expensive to go abroad, so if you do not have any savings prior, it is a very good idea to apply for these. I found all my mine via
KU.net
and
Legatbogen.dk
.

questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experience of living and studying abroad. It was so cool to try something else!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The coordination and setting up everything yourself.
